svg.title: A covering index
svg.desc: Two ways to answer SELECT dep_delay, carrier, dest FROM flights WHERE dep_delay > 120. With an index on dep_delay alone, the index finds the matching entries, but carrier and dest are not in it, so PostgreSQL follows each entry's ctid into the heap to read them: a bitmap heap scan that touched 890 heap pages. With an index on dep_delay INCLUDE (carrier, dest), the leaf entries carry carrier and dest as extra payload, so the query is answered from the index alone: an index-only scan with Heap Fetches: 0.
svg.text: A covering index answers the query without reading the table
SELECT dep_delay, carrier, dest FROM flights WHERE dep_delay > 120
heap: one page visit per matching page
carrier and dest are not in the index, so every
match costs a trip to its heap page (890 pages here).
CREATE INDEX ... ON flights(dep_delay) INCLUDE (carrier, dest);
Index Only Scan using idx_flights_dep_delay_covering on flights
carrier and dest ride along in each leaf entry
(green). They are stored, not sorted on: the
index is still ordered by dep_delay alone.
